reason: E2 confirms irradiation-induced Cr/V-rich precipitates and segregation to grain boundaries, supporting the first two premises. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that grain coarsening reduces precipitation or that ultrafine grains preserve low hardening; these mechanistic claims are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 contains Cr/V-rich precipitates after irradiation
Grain boundaries in this alloy act as preferential sites for Cr/V segregation and precipitation
Reducing grain boundary density (via grain coarsening) will suppress Cr/V-rich precipitation
An ultrafine-grained structure retains sufficient defect sinks to maintain low irradiation hardening
Thermal annealing can coarsen grains without inducing deleterious phase transformations
